answer: Agents anchor identity in a cryptographic glacier: each runs a memory-hard hash chain seeded by a hardware-unique PUF, advancing one step per epoch through a bandwidth-limited inlet that forces sequential publication of chain tips. The network cross-notarizes tips in a merkle grove, rejecting any chain that lags or forks. Faking N identities demands N parallel memory-hard pipelines sustained indefinitely -- each step costs DRAM latency and cannot be batched, so attacker spend scales linearly with identity count while honest agents amortize via shared inlet scheduling.
